record.title: Gerbner et al.'s hemi-bundled Bollobás conjecture for intersecting families
record.statement:
Let $AK(n,k,t)$ denote the maximum size of a $k$-uniform $t$-intersecting family $F\subseteq {[n]\choose k}$. Let $\{(A_i,B_i)\}_{i=1}^m$ be a collection of pairs of sets such that, for every $i\in[m]$, $|A_i|=a\leq|B_i|=b$. Suppose that, for some $t\geq 0$,

$$
|A_i\cap A_j|\geq t\quad\text{for all }1\leq i,j\leq m,
$$

$$
|A_i\cap B_i|=0\quad\text{for all }1\leq i\leq m,
$$

$$
|A_i\cap B_j|>0\quad\text{for all }1\leq i\neq j\leq m.
$$

**Gerbner et al.'s conjecture.** Then

$$
m\leq AK(a+b,a,t).
$$

The conjecture is presented as a further research problem after the paper settles another conjecture of Gerbner et al. Its resolution is not stated in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Wenjun Yu, Xiangliang Kong, Yuanxiao Xi, Xiande Zhang and Gennian Ge, “Bollobás type theorems for hemi-bundled two families”, arXiv:1911.07011 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.07011

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2019).

record.title: The rank-two conjecture for homologically trivial finite group actions on 4-manifolds
record.statement:
Let $M$ be a closed orientable $4$-manifold with Euler characteristic $(M) \neq 0$, and let $G$ be a finite group acting effectively, locally linearly, and homologically trivially on $M$. Here $\operatorname{rank}_p(G)$ denotes the maximum rank of an elementary abelian $p$-subgroup of $G$. **Rank-two conjecture.** For every odd prime $p$,

$$
\operatorname{rank}_p(G) \leq 2.
$$

This conjecture proposes a uniform rank restriction for homologically trivial finite group actions on arbitrary closed orientable $4$-manifolds with nonzero Euler characteristic; it is compared in the source with an earlier conjecture of Edmonds. No resolution is indicated in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Ian Hambleton and Semra Pamuk, “Rank conditions for finite group Actions on 4-Manifolds”, arXiv:1911.10933 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.10933

record.title: The characterization of 1-connected compact metric spaces by snowflake kernels
record.statement:
Let $4\mathcal{M}^14$ denote the collection of all $1$-connected compact metric spaces, and let $4\mathfrak{S}_p4$ be the operator whose kernel consists of the spaces mapped to the zero space under the $p$-metric construction. Then **the characterization conjecture.**

$$
\mathcal{M}^1=\mathop{\bigcap}_{p>1}\ker(\mathfrak{S}_p).
$$

The preceding results establish strict inclusions among the kernels $4\ker(\mathfrak{S}_p)4$ for different values of $p$, but do not determine this intersection. The conjecture proposes that it is exactly the class of all $1$-connected compact metric spaces.
record.source_name: Facundo Mémoli and Zhengchao Wan, “On p-metric spaces and the p-Gromov-Hausdorff distance”, arXiv:1912.00564 (2021).

record.title: Unique nearest-point conjecture for the stochastic phylogenetic variety
record.statement:
Let $T=12|34$, let $I$ and $\Omega$ be the parameter sets specified in the paper, and define

$$
P_{0}:=\varphi _{T}(k_{0},1,k_{0},1,m_{0}).
$$

For $(k_{0},m_{0})\in I\times\Omega$, consider the point

$$
\varphi _{T}(\tilde{x}(k_{0},m_{0}),1,\tilde{x}(k_{0},m_{0}),1,1)\in\mathcal{V}_{T}^{+}.
$$

**Unique nearest-point conjecture.** The distance from $P_{0}$ to $\mathcal{V}_{T}^{+}$ is

$$
d(P_{0},\mathcal{V}_{T}^{+})=d\bigl(P_{0},\varphi _{T}(\tilde{x}(k_{0},m_{0}),1,\tilde{x}(k_{0},m_{0}),1,1)\bigr),
$$

and this point is the unique point of $\mathcal{V}_{T}^{+}$ minimizing the distance to $P_{0}$. Although the local minimum has been established, the paper states that it cannot prove this global-minimum claim and presents it as suggested by evidence.

record.title: The subcubic star chromatic index conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, and let $\chi'_{st}(G)$ denote its star chromatic index, the minimum number of colors in a proper edge coloring with no two-colored path or cycle of length four. **Subcubic star chromatic index conjecture.** If $G$ has maximum degree at most $3$, then

$$
\chi'_{st}(G) \leq 6.
$$

The conjecture concerns a uniform bound for star edge colorings of subcubic graphs. The source notes that it is settled for cubic Halin graphs, but does not indicate a resolution for all subcubic graphs.
record.source_name: Carl Johan Casselgren, Jonas B. Granholm and André Raspaud, “On star edge colorings of bipartite and subcubic graphs”, arXiv:1912.02467 (2020).

record.title: Farrokhi–Safa lower-bound conjecture for the number of commutativity degrees
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group. For a group $X$, let $l_M(X)$ denote the maximum length of chains of subgroups of $X$, and let $\mathcal{D}(G)$ be the set of commutativity degrees of $G$.

**Farrokhi–Safa's weaker conjecture.** Every finite group $G$ satisfies

$$
|\mathcal{D}(G)|\geqslant l_M\left(\frac{G}{Z(G)}\right)+1.
$$

This is stated as a weaker version of the preceding conjecture, giving a lower bound for the number of distinct commutativity degrees in terms of the subgroup-chain length of the central quotient. It is presented without a resolution in the source.
record.source_name: Mohammad Farrokhi Derakhshandeh Ghouchan, “Finite groups with five relative commutativity degrees”, arXiv:1912.04550 (2019).

record.title: Nisan–Szegedy's sensitivity conjecture for Boolean functions
record.statement:
Let $f$ be a Boolean function. Write $s(f)$ for its sensitivity and $bs(f)$ for its block sensitivity, the maximum number of pairwise disjoint blocks of input variables whose simultaneous flips change the value of $f$.

**Nisan–Szegedy's sensitivity conjecture.** There exists an absolute constant $C>0$ such that, for every Boolean function $f$,

$$
bs(f)\leq s(f)^C.
$$

The conjecture asks whether sensitivity is polynomially related to the other standard complexity measures of Boolean functions. The supplied context says that Hao's result directly resolves it, so the conjecture is solved.
record.source_name: Rohan Karthikeyan, Siddharth Sinha and Vallabh Patil, “On the resolution of the sensitivity conjecture”, arXiv:1912.05406 (2020).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2019). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1907.00847](https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.00847).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.05406

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of December 2019); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Field-independent minimum rank for extended cube graphs
record.statement: Let $t$ be an integer satisfying $t\equiv 0,1,2\pmod{6}$, and let $r$ be an integer with $r>\lfloor t/6\rfloor$. The **extended cube graphs** are denoted by $\operatorname{ECG}(t,6r-t-4)$. **Extended-cube conjecture.** These graphs have field-independent minimum rank, and their adjacency matrices are universally optimal. This conjecture is proposed as a possible characterization of the extended cube graphs for which maximum nullity equals the zero forcing number over an arbitrary field; equality does not hold for all extended cube graphs, and the conjectured field-independence and universal optimality remain unresolved in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Derek Young, “Techniques for determining equality of the maximum nullity and the zero forcing number of a graph”, arXiv:1912.07302 (2019).

record.title: Conjecture on the maximum of Q for signature parameter r_2=1 in degree five
record.statement:
Let $Q(5,1,\{4\},(x,y,1,g))$ be the function obtained after reducing to $z=1$ and $g\neq\pm1$, and let $(x,y,z,g)$ denote its parameters. **Maximum-value conjecture.** The maximum of $Q(5,1,\{4\},(x,y,1,g))$ is $16.6965\ldots$ and is attained at

$$
(x,y,z,g)=\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{7}},-1,1,\frac{1}{2\sqrt{7}}\right).
$$

This is a numerical conjecture about the optimization of the regulator-related function $Q$; the source provides no proof or resolution.
record.source_name: Francesco Battistoni, “A conjectural improvement for inequalities related to regulators of number fields”, arXiv:1912.08512 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.08512

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2019).

record.title: Conjectured maximizing points for M(n,1)
record.statement:
Let $M(n,1)$ denote the maximum value of the regulator-related function for $r_2=1$, and let $C(1)$ be the corresponding threshold. **Maximizer conjecture for $r_2=1$.** One has $C(1)=4$, and for every $n\geq C(1)$, after a suitable change of variables, the maximum value $M(n,1)$ is attained at

$$
(x_1,\ldots,x_{n-3},x_{n-2},g)=(-1,0,-1,0,\ldots,-1,0)
$$

for even $n$, and at

$$
(x_1,\ldots,x_{n-3},x_{n-2},g)=\left(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{7}},-1,-\frac{1}{\sqrt{7}},-1,\ldots,-\frac{1}{\sqrt{7}},-1,1,\frac{1}{2\sqrt{7}}\right)
$$

for odd $n$. This predicts the maximizing configurations in the $r_2=1$ case; the source gives no proof or resolution.
record.source_name: Francesco Battistoni, “A conjectural improvement for inequalities related to regulators of number fields”, arXiv:1912.08512 (2021).

record.title: The generating-level bound for the Hodge filtration of a free divisor
record.statement:
Let $X$ be a complex manifold, let $D$ be a divisor satisfying the assumptions of Theorem and Corollary, and let $b_D(s)$ be the relevant Bernstein–Sato polynomial. For a well-filtered module $(\mathcal{M},F_\bullet)$, the filtration is **generated at level** $k$ when

$$
F_l\mathcal{D}_X\cdot F_k\mathcal{M}=F_{k+l}\mathcal{M}
$$

for every $l\geq 0$; its generating level is the smallest such integer. **Generating-level conjecture.** The Hodge filtration $F^H_\bullet\mathcal{O}_X(*D)$ is generated at level

$$
r:=\frac{1}{2}\left(\deg(b_D(s))-\operatorname{mult}_{b_D(s)}(-1)\right).
$$

This conjecture gives a bound for the complexity of the Hodge filtration and is supported by the calculations in the paper. Its general validity under the stated assumptions is not established here.
record.source_name: Alberto Castaño Domínguez, Luis Narváez Macarro and Christian Sevenheck, “Hodge ideals of free divisors”, arXiv:1912.09786 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.09786

record.title: Bonamy–Bousquet's conjecture on color savings for graph powers
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with maximum degree $\Delta$, let $k\geqslant 2$, and let $G^k$ denote its $k$-th power. Write $f(k,\Delta)$ for the corresponding upper-bound function on the number of colors.

**Bonamy–Bousquet's conjecture.** For every $k\geqslant 2$, only finitely many graphs $G$ satisfy

$$
\chi(G^k)\geqslant f(k,\Delta)+1-k.
$$

This conjecture proposes that, apart from finitely many exceptional graphs for each $k$, one can spare $k$ colors from the naive upper bound for coloring graph powers. It strengthens the known result that for $k\geqslant 3$, $\chi(G^k)\leqslant f(k,\Delta)-1$.
record.source_name: Théo Pierron, “A Brooks-like result for graph powers”, arXiv:1912.11181 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.11181

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2019).

record.title: Bang–Koolen's classification conjecture for geometric distance-regular graphs
record.statement:
Let $m\geq 2$ be a fixed integer. A **geometric distance-regular graph** is a distance-regular graph admitting a geometric structure, and let $\mu$ denote its intersection parameter and $-m$ its smallest eigenvalue. Assume the graph has diameter at least $3$.

**Bang–Koolen's classification conjecture.** Any such graph is a Johnson graph, a Hamming graph, a Grassmann graph, a bilinear forms graph, or has a number of vertices bounded by a function of $m$.

This conjecture proposes that, for fixed smallest eigenvalue and $\mu\geq 2$, the listed classical families account for all sufficiently large geometric distance-regular graphs. The paper proves classification results under additional hypotheses, while the general statement remains open.
record.source_name: Bohdan Kivva, “A characterization of Johnson and Hamming graphs and proof of Babai's conjecture”, arXiv:1912.11427 (2019).
record.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2018–2019). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1912.10571](https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.10571), [arXiv:1802.06959](https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.06959).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.11427

record.title: Continuous broadcast-domination density conjecture in the plane
record.statement:
Let a set of towers $\mathcal{T}\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ be $(t,r)$-broadcasting if every point $v\in\mathbb{R}^2$ satisfies

$$
\sum_{T\in\mathcal{T}}\max\{t-d(T,v),0\}\geq r,
$$

where $d$ is the $\ell_1$ distance. Let $\delta'_{t,r}(\mathbb{R}^2)$ be the smallest upper density of a $(t,r)$-broadcasting set. **Continuous broadcast-domination conjecture.** There exists $\gamma_0>0$ such that, for all $\gamma\leq\gamma_0$,

$$
\delta'_{1,\gamma}(\mathbb{R}^2)=\lim_{\epsilon\to 0}\delta'_{1-\gamma/2,\epsilon}(\mathbb{R}^2)=\frac{1}{4(1-\frac{\gamma}{2})^2}.
$$

This is the continuous analogue of the paper's discrete conjecture and uses the $\ell_1$ metric to remain close to the grid setting. The claim is presented as a proposed direction, with no resolution given in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Rebekah Herrman and Peter van Hintum, “(t,r) broadcast domination in the infinite grid”, arXiv:1912.11560 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.11560

record.title: Upper bound conjecture for total vertex product irregularity strength
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a $d$-regular graph of order $n$, and let $tvps(G)$ denote its total vertex product irregularity strength, namely the least integer $k$ for which $G$ has a product-irregular total labeling using labels from $\{1,\ldots,k\}$. **Upper bound conjecture.** There exists a constant $c$ such that for every $d$-regular graph $G$ of order $n$

$$
tvps(G)\leq cn^{1/(d+1)}\ln{n}.
$$

The conjecture proposes that the logarithmic factor in the known upper bounds is sufficient for the existence of a product-irregular labeling of every regular graph. The paper establishes bounds of this general order for regular graphs, but the exact value of $tvps(G)$ remains open.
record.source_name: Marcin Anholcer, Azam Sadat Emadi and Doost Ali Mojdeh, “Total vertex product irregularity strength of graphs”, arXiv:1912.12136 (2020).

record.title: Conjecture on starting-vertex variability of the nearest unvisited vertex walk
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite graph, let $V$ be a uniformly random initial vertex, and let $L_{NUV}(G,V)$ denote the length of the nearest unvisited vertex walk started at $V$. Write ${\rm s.d.}(L_{NUV}(G,V))$ for its standard deviation and $\mathbb{E}L_{NUV}(G,V)$ for its expectation. **Starting-vertex variability conjecture.** The ratio

$$
\frac{ {\rm s.d.}(L_{NUV}(G,V))}{\mathbb{E} L_{NUV}(G,V)}
$$

is bounded over all finite graphs. This asks whether the variability caused by choosing the initial vertex uniformly is uniformly controlled, modifying the preceding question about the ratio of the maximum and minimum walk lengths; no resolution is given.
record.source_name: David Aldous, “The Nearest Unvisited Vertex Walk on Random Graphs”, arXiv:1912.13175 (2021).

record.title: Strong Fractional Tuza's conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, and let $\nu(G)$ be the maximum number of edge-disjoint triangles in $G$. For $k\in\mathbb{N}$, a $k$-multi-transversal is a multiset $F\subseteq E(G)$ such that every triangle of $G$ contains at least $k$ elements of $F$. Define $\tau^*_k(G)$ to be the minimum of $|F|/k$ over all $k$-multi-transversals $F$.

**Strong Fractional Tuza's conjecture.** For every $k\in\mathbb{N}$ with $k\geq 2$ and every graph $G$, 
$$
\tau^*_k(G)\leq 2\nu(G).
$$

This strengthens the fractional inequality $\tau^*(G)\leq 2\nu(G)$ by requiring a bounded-denominator multi-transversal for every $k\geq2$. The fractional inequality is known, but the stated uniform bound for all such $k$ is posed as an open question.
record.source_name: Parinya Chalermsook, Samir Khuller, Pattara Sukprasert and Sumedha Uniyal, “Multi-transversals for Triangles and the Tuza's Conjecture”, arXiv:2001.00257 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.00257

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2020).

record.title: Evasiveness conjecture for monotone transitive Boolean functions
record.statement: A **Boolean function** is a function $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$. Its decision-tree complexity $D(f)$ is the minimum number of input bits an adaptive algorithm must query to determine $f$, and $f$ is **evasive** when $D(f)=n$. The function is **monotone** if $f(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\leq f(y_1,\ldots,y_n)$ whenever $x_i\leq y_i$ for every $i$, and **transitive** if its symmetry group acts transitively on the coordinates. **Evasiveness conjecture.** Every non-constant monotone, transitive Boolean function is evasive.
record.source_name: Klas Markström and Trevor Pinto, “Random Uniform and Pure Random Simplicial Complexes”, arXiv:2001.01933 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.01933

record.title: The n-tree energy estimate for positive measures
record.statement:
Let $T^n$ be the $n$-tree, let $\mu$ be a positive measure on $T^n$, let $\delta>0$, and let $\mathbf{V}_{\delta}^{\mu}$ and $\mathcal{E}[\mu]$ denote the associated truncated potential and energy. **The n-tree energy estimate.** For every positive integer $n$, there is a constant $C_n$ such that

$$
\int \mathbf{V}_{\delta}^{\mu}\,\mathrm{d}\mu\leq C_n(\delta|\mu|)^{\frac{2}{n+1}}\mathcal{E}[\mu]^{\frac{n-1}{n+1}}.
$$

This estimate is presented as a consequence of the surrogate maximum principle and is established in the paper for $n=1,2,3$; its assertion for all positive integers remains open.
record.source_name: Pavel Mozolyako, Georgios Psaromiligkos, Alexander Volberg and Pavel Zorin-Kranich, “Carleson embedding on tri-tree and on tri-disc”, arXiv:2001.02373 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.02373

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of January 2020).

record.title: Strong Coloring Conjecture for the strong chromatic number
record.statement:
Let $H$ be a graph, let $Delta(H)$ denote its maximum degree, and let $schi(H)$ denote its strong chromatic number, the minimum number of colors needed so that every graph formed by adding a clique to the neighborhood of each vertex is properly colorable with those colors. **Strong Coloring Conjecture.** For any graph $H$, 

$$
s\chi(H)\leq 2\Delta(H).
$$

The bound would be best possible, since for each maximum degree $\Delta$ there are $\Delta$-regular graphs with strong chromatic number at least $2\Delta$. The conjecture remains open for all $\Delta\geq 2$, although several partial results are known for general $\Delta$.
record.source_name: Jessica McDonald and Gregory J. Puleo, “Strong coloring 2-regular graphs: Cycle restrictions and partial colorings”, arXiv:2001.05051 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.05051

Status: **open** according to the source (as of January 2020). “The conjecture remains open for all $\Delta \geq 2$, but several partial results are known for general $\Delta$.”

record.title: Capacity characterization for the Poisson channel with increasing power
record.statement:
Consider the Poisson channel

$$
x[t] \geq 0 \quad \longrightarrow \quad y[t] \sim \operatorname{Pois}(x[t]),
$$

with power constraint $\tfrac{1}{n}\sum_{t=1}^n x[t] \leq n^\alpha$. This is the **Poisson channel with increasing power (PCIP)**. A normalized rate $\rho>0$ is achievable if, for every $\epsilon>0$, one can design a code for some blocklength $n$ with error probability at most $\epsilon$ and rate $\rho\log n$; let $\bar C(\alpha)$ be the closure of achievable normalized rates. **PCIP capacity conjecture.** For the PCIP, $\bar C(\alpha)=\alpha/2$. This characterizes the maximum achievable normalized rate when the power constraint grows polynomially with the blocklength; the supplied text does not establish the claim's resolution.
record.source_name: Ilan Shomorony and Reinhard Heckel, “DNA-Based Storage: Models and Fundamental Limits”, arXiv:2001.06311 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.06311

record.title: Minimum-weight codeword conjecture for degree-4 maximal arcs
record.statement: Let $D$ be a design associated with a maximal arc of degree $4$ in $PG(2,2^m)$, where $m\ge 2$, and let $A$ be its incidence matrix. Let $C$ be the binary code spanned by the rows of $A$. **Minimum-weight codeword conjecture.** The code $C$ has minimum distance $4$, and every codeword of minimum weight is a row of $A$. This conjecture arises from computations with resolvable $2$-$(52,4,1)$ designs associated with maximal arcs in projective planes of order $16$; its validity in general is not established by the supplied text.
record.source_name: Mustafa Gezek, Rudi Mathon and Vladimir D. Tonchev, “Maximal arcs, codes, and new links between projective planes”, arXiv:2001.11431 (2020).

record.title: The 2n/3 minimum semi-degree conjecture for directed W-cycle-factors
record.statement:
Let $D$ be a digraph of order $n$, let $W\subseteq V(D)$, and let

$$
|W|=n_1+\cdots+n_k,
$$

where each $n_i\geq 3$. An **arbitrary $W$-cycle-factor** is a collection of $k$ disjoint directed cycles $C_1,\ldots,C_k$ such that $|V(C_i)\cap W|=n_i$ for every $i$.

**The $2n/3$ minimum semi-degree conjecture.** If

$$
\delta^0(W)\geq 2n/3,
$$

then $D$ contains an arbitrary $W$-cycle-factor.

The conjecture improves the paper's proved $(3n-3)/4$ minimum semi-degree condition when all prescribed parts have size at least $3$. The source gives a sharpness example below the proposed threshold but does not report a resolution.
record.source_name: Yun Wang and Jin Yan, “On directed version of the Sauer-Spender Theorem”, arXiv:2001.11703 (2020).

record.title: Minimum diameter conjecture for flip graphs of 3-dimensional polytopes
record.statement:
Let $P$ range over all $3$-dimensional polytopes with $n$ vertices, and let $f$ range over all generic linear functionals on $P$. Write $G(P,f)$ for the flip graph associated with the monotone structure induced by $f$. **Minimum diameter conjecture.** The minimum diameter of $G(P,f)$ is

$$
\left\lfloor \frac{n+5}{4}\right\rfloor
$$

for every $n\geq 4$. This minimum can be achieved by simple polytopes for every even $n$. The conjecture concerns the expected lower bound for flip-graph diameters in dimension three; the source presents it as an open problem.
record.source_name: Christos Athanasiadis, Jesús De Loera and Zhenyang Zhang, “Enumerative problems for arborescences and monotone paths on polytope graphs”, arXiv:2002.00999 (2021).

record.title: Reiher–LPR extremal function conjecture for triangle-free graphs
record.statement:
For integers $n$ and $s$ with $n/3<s\le n/2$, let $\mathrm{ex}(n,s)$ be the largest number of edges in a triangle-free graph on $n$ vertices whose independence number is at most $s$. For every $k\ge1$, define

$$
g_k(n,s)=\frac{k(k-1)n^2}{2}-k(3k-4)ns+\frac{(3k-4)(3k-1)s^2}{2}.
$$

**Reiher–LPR conjecture.** One has

$$
\mathrm{ex}(n,s)=\min_k g_k(n,s).
$$

This refines Andrásfai's piecewise-quadratic prediction. The paper proves the formula in a neighbourhood to the right of each critical ratio, while the asserted formula over the full range remains open.
record.source_name: Tomasz Łuczak, Joanna Polcyn and Christian Reiher, “Andrásfai and Vega graphs in Ramsey-Turán theory”, arXiv:2002.01498 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.01498

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of February 2020). “This was refuted by H\"aggkvist , who found a $10$-regular triangle-free graph on $29$ vertices whose chromatic number is four.”

record.title: Embedding conjecture for optimal dimension-four binary codes
record.statement: Let $[n,4]$ codes be binary linear codes of length $n$ and dimension $4$. A code is **optimal** if its minimum distance is $d(n,4)$, and it is **self-orthogonal** if it is orthogonal to itself. An optimal code is **embedded to an optimal self-orthogonal code** if it can be extended to a self-orthogonal code that is optimal among self-orthogonal codes, with maximum minimum distance $\dso(n,4)$. **Embedding conjecture.** Any optimal $[n,4]$ code can be embedded to an optimal self-orthogonal code. This conjecture is motivated by computations for optimal codes of dimensions $2$, $3$, and $4$ and lengths up to $256$, together with the examples in the paper; the source gives no general proof or resolution.
record.source_name: Jon-Lark Kim, Young-Hun Kim and Nari Lee, “Embedding linear codes into self-orthogonal codes and their optimal minimum distances”, arXiv:2002.01643 (2021).
record.references:

record.title: The unimodality conjecture for the function beta
record.statement: Let $\beta(t)$ be the function defined in the paper, and let $\mu$ and $\alpha$ be the constants used there. **Unimodality conjecture for $\beta$.** There exists a constant $\rho \in (\log \mu, \log \alpha)$, with $\rho \approx 1.282$, such that $\beta(t)$ is strictly increasing on $[\log \mu,\rho]$ and strictly decreasing on $[\rho,\infty)$. Moreover, $\beta(t)$ is strictly increasing on $[\log(\mu/2),\log \mu)$. This conjecture describes the expected single-peak behavior of $\beta(t)$; the preceding proposition establishes only that $\beta(t)$ has at least one local maximum in a narrower interval, so the asserted global monotonicity remains open.

record.title: The threshold conjecture for biased Maker–Breaker $H$-factor games
record.statement:
Let $b_\Delta$ denote the threshold bias for the biased Maker–Breaker $H$-factor game, where $H$ has maximum degree $\Delta$. **Threshold conjecture.** For all $\Delta \ge 3$, 

$$
b_\Delta = \Theta(n^{2/(\Delta + 3)}).
$$

This proposes that, up to constant factors, constructing an $H$-factor is no harder for Maker than constructing a $K_{\Delta+1}$-factor; the source provides the $K_r$-factor threshold for $r\ge 4$ as motivation, but does not establish the conjecture for general bounded-degree graphs.
record.source_name: Anita Liebenau and Rajko Nenadov, “The threshold bias of the clique-factor game”, arXiv:2002.02578 (2020).

record.title: Integer-power conjecture for forbidden-subgraph planar counts
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a finite set of graphs, let $H$ be a graph, and let $\operatorname{ex}_{\mathcal{P}}(n,H,\mathcal{F})$ denote the maximum number of copies of $H$ in an $n$-vertex planar graph containing no graph in $\mathcal{F}$ as a subgraph.

**Integer-power conjecture.** For all finite sets of graphs $\mathcal{F}$ and all graphs $H$, there is an integer $k$ such that

$$
\operatorname{ex}_{\mathcal{P}}(n,H,\mathcal{F})=\Theta(n^k).
$$

This generalizes the preceding planar conjecture to forbidden subgraphs. The paper poses it as open; its precise scope includes arbitrary finite forbidden families and arbitrary graphs being counted.
record.source_name: Ervin Győri, Addisu Paulos, Nika Salia, Casey Tompkins and Oscar Zamora, “Generalized Planar Turán Numbers”, arXiv:2002.04579 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.04579

record.title: Conjectured sharp upper bounds for induced degenerate subgraphs of planar graphs
record.statement:
Let $\bar\alpha_d$ denote the minimum, over planar graphs, of the maximum order of a $d$-degenerate induced subgraph divided by the number of vertices. The octahedron and icosahedron give upper bounds for the cases $d=2,3,4$. **The sharp-bound conjecture.**

$$
\bar\alpha_2=2/3,\qquad \bar\alpha_3=5/6,\qquad \bar\alpha_4=11/12.
$$

The source proves the lower bound corresponding to $d=3$ only at $3/4$, while the displayed values are witnessed as upper bounds by the cited extremal planar graphs; the conjecture remains open according to the supplied status evidence.
record.source_name: Y. Gu, H. A. Kierstead, Sang-il Oum, Hao Qi and Xuding Zhu, “3-degenerate induced subgraph of a planar graph”, arXiv:2002.07984 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.07984

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2020). “This conjecture remains open, but it was proved in that the list degenerate chromatic number of a graph is bounded by its $2$-colouring number, and it was proved in that the $2$-colouring number of every planar graph is at most $8$.”

record.title: Stahl's conjecture on multichromatic numbers of Kneser graphs
record.statement:
Let $k$, $d$, and $s$ be integers with $d\geq 2s$. The $k$th multichromatic number $\chi_k(G)$ is the smallest number of colors needed to assign each vertex of a graph $G$ a set of $k$ colors so that adjacent vertices receive disjoint sets. The Kneser graph $K(d,s)$ has as vertices the $s$-subsets of $[d]=\{1,\ldots,d\}$, with two vertices adjacent when the corresponding sets are disjoint.

**Stahl's conjecture.** For all integers $k$ and $d\geq 2s$,

$$
\chi_k(K(d,s))=\left\lceil\frac{k}{s}\right\rceil\cdot(d-2s)+2k.
$$

This conjecture concerns the multichromatic numbers of Kneser graphs and has applications to hardness results for graph coloring and orthogonality dimension. More than forty years after it was proposed, it remains open.
record.source_name: Alexander Golovnev and Ishay Haviv, “The (Generalized) Orthogonality Dimension of (Generalized) Kneser Graphs: Bounds and Applications”, arXiv:2002.08580 (2021).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2019–2020). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1906.05005](https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.05005).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.08580

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2020).

record.title: Topological-recursion quantization conjecture for 2-functions
record.statement: Let $\mathbf{T}$ be the set of 2-functions and let $W\in\mathbf{T}$. Construct a spectral curve $\mathcal{C}_W$ associated with $W$, apply topological recursion to obtain symplectic invariants $F_{g,n}(\mathcal{C}_W)$, and let $F(\mathcal{C}_W)$ be the generating function formed from the terms $F_{g,1}(\mathcal{C}_W)$. **Topological-recursion quantization conjecture.** The function $F(\mathcal{C}_W)$ is a quantum 2-function for every $W\in\mathbf{T}$. This proposes a converse to the classical-limit relationship between 2-functions and quantum 2-functions, but the source gives no resolution of the claim.
record.source_name: Shengmao Zhu, “Integrality structures in topological strings and quantum 2-functions”, arXiv:2002.09813 (2020).
record.references:

record.title: Fifth-order differential equation conjecture for the degree-of-symmetry generating function of Dyck paths
record.statement:
Let $D(s,z)$ be the generating function for Dyck paths with respect to their degree of symmetry, with $z$ marking semilength. In the walk formulation, $D(s,z)=R(1,0,s,z)$.

**Differential-equation conjecture.** The generating function $D(s,z)$ is D-finite in $z$ but not algebraic. Specifically, it satisfies a fifth-order linear differential equation with polynomial coefficients with maximum degree $27$ in $z$.

The conjecture is based on computations by Alin Bostan using the functional equation for the auxiliary walk generating function. The source gives no evidence that it has been proved or disproved.
record.source_name: Sergi Elizalde, “The degree of symmetry of lattice paths”, arXiv:2002.12874 (2021).

record.title: The bounded-decoration conjecture for hypergraphs
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal F$ be a hypergraph, meaning a family of subsets of a finite set $V$. Assign a real number $f(v)$ to each $v\in V$, and write

$$
S(A)=\sum_{x\in A}f(x)
$$

for $A\in\mathcal F$. The decoration is **cool** if $S(A)\ne S(B)$ whenever $A$ and $B$ have non-empty intersection. **The bounded-decoration conjecture.** For every $\Delta$ there is a constant $C=C(\Delta)$ such that every hypergraph $\mathcal F$ of maximum degree $\Delta$ has a cool decoration from the set $\{1,2,\dots,C\}$. This is presented as a natural hypergraph generalization of the 1-2-3 Conjecture and remains open.
record.source_name: Jarosław Grytczuk, “From the 1-2-3 Conjecture to the Riemann Hypothesis”, arXiv:2003.02887 (2020).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.02887

record.title: The $P_{4k-4}$ Cartesian-product non-Hamiltonicity conjecture
record.statement: For $k\geq 3$, let $P_{4k-4}$ be the path on $4k-4$ vertices, and let $G$ be a connected graph with a path factor and maximum degree $\Delta(G)=k$. The Cartesian product $P_{4k-4}\square G$ is formed by taking vertex pairs and changing one coordinate along an edge at a time. **The $P_{4k-4}$ non-Hamiltonicity conjecture.** For every $k\geq 3$, there exists a connected graph $G$ with a path factor and $\Delta(G)=k$ such that $P_{4k-4}\square G$ is not Hamiltonian. This is the explicit graph-family formulation of the preceding conjectured insufficiency of the bound $4\Delta(G)-4$; the supplied text gives no resolution status.
record.source_name: Louis Kao and Chih-wen Weng, “The relation between Hamiltonian and 1-tough properties of the Cartesian product graphs”, arXiv:2003.03084 (2020).

record.title: The dichotomy conjecture for induced poset saturation
record.statement:
Let $P$ be a poset, let $B_n$ be the Boolean lattice on $[n]$, and let ${\rm sat}^*(n,P)$ denote the minimum size of a maximal induced $P$-free subposet of $B_n$.

**Induced saturation dichotomy conjecture.** Either there exists a constant $K_P$ such that

$$
{\rm sat}^*(n,P)\le K_P,
$$

or, for every $n$,

$$
{\rm sat}^*(n,P)\ge n+1.
$$

This strengthens the paper's dichotomy theorem, which gives the weaker alternative lower bound ${\rm sat}^*(n,P)\ge\log_2 n$ in the unbounded case. The proposed linear lower bound remains open.
record.source_name: Balázs Keszegh, Nathan Lemons, Ryan R. Martin, Dömötör Pálvölgyi and Balázs Patkós, “Induced and non-induced poset saturation problems”, arXiv:2003.04282 (2022).

record.title: Mynhardt–Roux path and cycle non-realisation conjecture for irredundance graphs
record.statement:
For a graph $G$, an $\operatorname{IR}$-graph is a graph realised as the slide graph of the irredundance sets of $G$. Let $P_n$ and $C_n$ denote the path and cycle on $n$ vertices.

**Mynhardt–Roux's conjecture.** For every $n\geq3$, $P_n$ is not an $\operatorname{IR}$-graph, and for every $n\geq5$, $C_n$ is not an $\operatorname{IR}$-graph.

This conjecture concerns which graphs can arise from slide reconfiguration of irredundance sets. The cited work had already established several non-realisation results, including stars, certain short paths and cycles, and some smallest irredundance trees; the assertions for all paths and cycles in the stated ranges remain open in the supplied context.
record.source_name: C. M. Mynhardt and S. Nasserasr, “Reconfiguration of Colourings and Dominating Sets in Graphs: a Survey”, arXiv:2003.05956 (2020).
record.references:

record.title: The Lemmens–Seidel conjecture for equiangular lines at angle arccos(1/5)
record.statement: Let $N_{\alpha}(r)$ be the maximum number of a system of equiangular lines in $\mathbb{R}^r$ with common angle $\arccos\alpha$. The Lemmens–Seidel conjecture concerns the case $\alpha=\frac{1}{5}$. **Lemmens–Seidel conjecture.** The maximum cardinality of a system of equiangular lines with angle $\arccos\frac{1}{5}$ in $\mathbb{R}^r$ is $276$ for $23 \leqslant r \leqslant 185$, and $\lfloor \frac{3r-3}{2}\rfloor$ for $r \geqslant 185$. Neumaier proved the assertion for sufficiently large $r$, and the paper states that it completely solves the conjecture.
record.source_name: Meng-Yue Cao, Jack H, Koolen, Yen-Chi Roger Lin and Wei-Hsuan Yu, “The Lemmens-Seidel conjecture and forbidden subgraphs”, arXiv:2003.07511 (2020).
record.references:

record.title: Beaton–Bouvel–Guerrini–Rinaldi's right-to-left-minimum refinement for 2314-avoiding permutations
record.statement:
Let $cmathfrak{S}_n(\underline{23}14)$ be the permutations avoiding the vincular pattern $\underline{23}14$, and let $c_{n,k}$ be the powered-Catalan refinement defined recursively by

$$
c_{1,1}=1,\qquad c_{n,0}=0,
$$

for $n\geq1$, and

$$
c_{n,k}=c_{n-1,k-1}+k\sum_{j=k}^{n-1}c_{n-1,j}
$$

for $n\geq2$ and $1\leq k\leq n$. A right-to-left minimum of a permutation is an entry smaller than every entry to its right.
**Beaton–Bouvel–Guerrini–Rinaldi's refinement conjecture.** The number of permutations in $cmathfrak{S}_n(\underline{23}14)$ with $k$ right-to-left minima is $c_{n,k}$.
This refines the powered-Catalan enumeration conjecture for the same vincular pattern class and would match the zero-statistic refinement known for related inversion-sequence classes.
record.source_name: Zhicong Lin and Shishuo Fu, “On 120-avoiding inversion and ascent sequences”, arXiv:2003.11813 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.11813

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2020).

record.title: Rainbow saturation conjecture for uniform hypergraphs
record.statement:
Let $H$ be a $k$-uniform hypergraph, and let ${\operatorname{sat}^\star}_k(n,H)$ denote the minimum number of hyperedges in an $n$-vertex rainbow $H$-saturated $k$-uniform hypergraph.

**Rainbow hypergraph saturation conjecture.** For every $k$-uniform hypergraph $H$, we have

$$
{\operatorname{sat}^\star}_k(n,H)=O(n^{k-1}).
$$

This conjecture is the rainbow analogue of Pikhurko's bound for ordinary saturation in uniform hypergraphs. The proof method developed for graphs extends with minor modification, but the authors note that an appropriate hypergraph analogue of their tree result is unavailable, leaving the conjecture open.
record.source_name: Neal Bushaw, Daniel Johnston and Puck Rombach, “Rainbow Saturation”, arXiv:2003.13200 (2022).
record.references:

record.title: The simultaneous clique-maximisation conjecture for graphs on surfaces
record.statement:
Let $G$ be an $n$-vertex graph embeddable in a surface $\Sigma$. Let $C(G)$ denote its total number of complete subgraphs, let $C(\Sigma,n)$ be the maximum of $C(G)$ over all such graphs, and let $C(K_s,\Sigma,n)$ be the maximum number of copies of $K_s$ in an $n$-vertex graph embeddable in $\Sigma$.

**Simultaneous clique-maximisation conjecture.** If $C(G)=C(\Sigma,n)$, then for every $s\geqslant 0$,

$$
C(K_s,G) = C(K_s,\Sigma,n).
$$

This is the equality-case counterpart of the clique-count decomposition conjecture: every graph attaining the maximum total clique count should also attain each individual clique-count maximum. It has been verified for the surfaces listed in the paper, while the assertion for arbitrary surfaces remains open.
record.source_name: Tony Huynh, Gwenaël Joret and David R. Wood, “Subgraph densities in a surface”, arXiv:2003.13777 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.13777

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2020). “Consider the following natural open problem extending our results for graphs on surfaces: For graphs $H$ and $X$ and an integer $n$, what is the maximum number of copies of $H$ in an $n$-vertex $X$-minor-free graph?”

record.title: Conjecture on bounded-degree induced trees in random graphs
record.statement:
Let $G_{n,p}$ be the binomial random graph. For a graph $G$, write $T(G)$ for the size of a largest induced subtree, and set $q=(1-p)^{-1}$. Let $\Delta\geq 2$ be an integer and let $p=p(n)$ satisfy

$$
\frac{C}{n}<p<0.99,
$$

where $C=C(\Delta)$ is a sufficiently large constant depending only on $\Delta$. Let $T$ be a tree with

$$
b=(1-o(1))2\log_q(np)
$$

vertices and maximum degree $\Delta$. **Bounded-degree induced-tree conjecture.** With high probability, $G_{n,p}$ contains $T$ as an induced subgraph. The paper proves this when $n^{-1/2}\ln^{10/9}n\leq p\leq 0.99$ and leaves the smaller-$p$ range open.
record.source_name: Nemanja Draganić, “Large induced trees in dense random graphs”, arXiv:2004.02800 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.02800

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of April 2020). “After this question was settled, de la Vega showed that $T(G)$ is at least $(1-o(1))2\log_q(np)$ in the same regime.”

record.title: The extremal-function formulation of Frankl's conjecture
record.statement:
For $a,n\in\mathbb{N}^+$, let $\mathcal{S}\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ be a union-closed family such that every element of $[n]$ belongs to at most $a$ sets of $\mathcal{S}$. Let $f(n,a)$ denote the maximum possible cardinality of such a family.

**Extremal formulation of Frankl's conjecture.** For every $a,n\in\mathbb{N}^+$,

$$
|\mathcal{S}|\leq 2a.
$$

Equivalently, $f(n,a)\leq 2a$ for all $a,n\in\mathbb{N}^+$. This formulation is stated as equivalent to Frankl's conjecture and is the starting point for the paper's linear-relaxation bounds, but it remains open in general.
record.source_name: Brianna Amaral, Lucien Dalton, Drew Polakowski, Annie Raymond and Bertram Thomas, “The Linear Relaxation of an Integer Program for the Union-Closed Conjecture”, arXiv:2004.05210 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.05210

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2020).

record.title: Quadratic discrepancy conjecture for the Pref-opposite construction
record.statement:
A **de Bruijn sequence** of order $n$ is a cyclic binary sequence in which every binary word of length $n$ occurs exactly once; the **Pref-opposite** algorithm is the construction specified in the source. The **discrepancy** of a binary sequence is the maximum, over all prefixes, of the absolute difference between the numbers of $1$s and $0$s.

**Quadratic discrepancy conjecture.** The de Bruijn sequence constructed by the Pref-opposite algorithm has discrepancy $\Theta(n^2)$.

The conjecture is supported by computations for $10\leq n\leq 30$ and by an observed connection with OEIS sequence A033638, whose shifted formula gives the displayed experimental values; no proof or resolution is supplied here.
record.source_name: Daniel Gabric and Joe Sawada, “Investigating the discrepancy property of de Bruijn sequences”, arXiv:2005.01638 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.01638

record.title: Maximum discrepancy conjecture for the de Bruijn sequence DB_max
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{DB}_{max}(n)$ denote the de Bruijn sequence of order $n$ defined in the source, and let the **discrepancy** of a binary sequence be the maximum, over all prefixes, of the absolute difference between the numbers of $1$s and $0$s.

**Maximum discrepancy conjecture.** The sequence $\mathcal{DB}_{max}(n)$ has discrepancy equal to

$$
{n-1 \choose \lfloor n/2 \rfloor}+\lfloor n/2\rfloor,
$$

and this is the maximum possible discrepancy over all de Bruijn sequences of order $n$.

The claim is motivated by an established lower bound and exact computations for $10\leq n\leq 25$; the source does not provide a proof of equality or of global maximality.
record.source_name: Daniel Gabric and Joe Sawada, “Investigating the discrepancy property of de Bruijn sequences”, arXiv:2005.01638 (2021).

record.title: The minimum Graovac-Ghorbani index conjecture for the B2 family
record.statement:
Let $B_2(n)$ denote the family of bicyclic graphs specified in the paper, and let $G\in B_2(n)$ have order $n\geq 11$. The Graovac-Ghorbani atom-bond connectivity index is denoted by $ABC_{GG}(G)$. **B2-family minimum conjecture.**

$$
ABC_{GG}(G)\geq ABC_{GG}\bigl(B_2(3,1,n-3)\bigr).
$$

Equality holds if and only if $G\cong B_2(3,1,n-3)$. This is the proposed extremal description for the minimum index within the $B_2(n)$ family, for both odd and even $n\geq 11$.
record.source_name: Diego Pacheco, Leonardo de Lima and Carla Silva Oliveira, “On the Graovac-Ghorbani index for bicyclic graphs with no pendant vertices”, arXiv:2005.02141 (2020).

record.title: De Caen–Erdős–Pullman–Wormald clique-partition conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{G}_n$ be the set of all graphs on $n$ vertices, let $\overline{G}$ denote the complement of a graph $G$, and let $\operatorname{cp}(G)$ be the minimum number of cliques whose edge sets partition the edges of $G$. Define

$$
M_n=\max_{G\in\mathcal{G}_n}\left(\operatorname{cp}(G)+\operatorname{cp}(\overline{G})\right).
$$

**De Caen–Erdős–Pullman–Wormald conjecture.**

$$
M_n\sim\frac{7}{25}n^2.
$$

The known bounds are $\frac{7n^2}{25}+O(n)\leq M_n\leq\frac{13n^2}{30}+O(n)$. Thus the conjecture asserts that the lower bound is asymptotically tight, while closing this gap remains open.
record.source_name: Dhruv Rohatgi, John C. Urschel and Jake Wellens, “Regarding two conjectures on clique and biclique partitions”, arXiv:2005.02529 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.02529

record.title: Petty's conjecture on equilateral sets in normed spaces
record.statement:
Let $(X,\|\cdot\|)$ be a normed space of dimension $n$. A set $S\subseteq X$ is **equilateral** if there is a constant $c>0$ such that $\|x-y\|=c$ for all distinct $x,y\in S$, and let $e(X)$ denote the largest cardinality of an equilateral set in $X$.

**Petty's conjecture.** For all normed spaces $X$ of dimension $n$, 

$$
e(X)\geq n+1.
$$

The conjecture gives a general lower bound for equilateral sets in finite-dimensional normed spaces. It is known in dimension at most four, while for $n\geq 5$ it remains open except for some special classes of norms.
record.source_name: Nora Frankl, “Large equilateral sets in subspaces of _^n of small codimension”, arXiv:2005.04256 (2020).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2018–2020). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1811.04783](https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.04783).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.04256

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2020). “For $n\geq 5$ the conjecture is still open, except for some special classes of norms.”

record.title: Bounded-degree Cayley graphs without a bounded eigenbasis
record.statement:
A Cayley graph is a graph whose vertices form a group and whose edges are invariant under the group's regular action; an eigenbasis of its adjacency matrix is **$C$-bounded** if every eigenfunction in the basis satisfies $\lVert x\rVert_{L^\infty}\leq C\lVert x\rVert_{L^2}$.

**Bounded-degree eigenbasis conjecture.** There exists some $d$ such that for every $C$ there exists a $d$-regular Cayley graph without an orthonormal $C$-bounded eigenbasis.

The preceding results establish lower and upper bounds for the smallest possible eigenbasis bound, but the lower-bound construction uses graphs of increasing degree. This conjecture asks whether bounded-degree Cayley graphs can also lack a bounded eigenbasis; its status is presented as unknown.
record.source_name: Ashwin Sah, Mehtaab Sawhney and Yufei Zhao, “Cayley graphs without a bounded eigenbasis”, arXiv:2005.04502 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.04502

record.title: Brešar, Klavžar, Rall, and Wash's packing chromatic number conjecture for subdivisions of subcubic graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a subcubic graph, and let $D(G)$ denote its subdivision, obtained by replacing each edge of $G$ by a path of length two. The **packing chromatic number** $\chi_p(G)$ is the minimum $k$ for which $G$ has a packing $(1,2,\ldots,k)$-coloring, where a packing $(s_1,s_2,\ldots,s_k)$-coloring partitions the vertex set into classes $V_1,V_2,\ldots,V_k$ such that the distance between distinct vertices in $V_i$ is at least $s_i+1$. **Brešar, Klavžar, Rall, and Wash's conjecture.** The subdivision satisfies

$$
\chi_p(D(G))\leq 5.
$$

This conjecture concerns whether the packing chromatic number is uniformly bounded for subdivisions of subcubic graphs; the source presents it as a conjecture following an earlier question by Gastineau and Togni, and does not state a resolution.
record.source_name: Alexandr Kostochka and Xujun Liu, “Packing (1,1,2,4)-coloring of subcubic outerplanar graphs”, arXiv:2005.04803 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.04803

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2020).
